t.17.1: Arjuna said: Those who, setting aside the ordinances of scripture, offer sacrifice endowed with faith, what is their standing, O Kṛṣṇa? Is it sattva, or rajas, or tamas?
t.17.2: The Blessed Lord said: The faith of embodied beings is of three kinds, born of their own nature: sāttvic, rājasic, and tāmasic. Hear about it.
t.17.3: The faith of each person, O Bhārata, is in accordance with his nature. This person is made of faith; whatever his faith is, that indeed is he.
t.17.4: Those of sāttvika nature worship the gods; those of rājasa nature worship the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas; and the others, people of tāmasa nature, worship the departed spirits and the hosts of ghosts.
t.17.5: Those people who practice terrible austerity not enjoined by the scriptures, joined with hypocrisy and egoism, and possessed of the force of desire and passion,
t.17.6: Senseless, they torment the aggregate of elements dwelling in the body, and Me also, who dwell within the body; know them to be of demoniac resolve.
t.17.7: Even the food that is dear to everyone is of three kinds, and so too are sacrifice, austerity and giving. Hear now this distinction among them.
t.17.8: Foods that increase life, vitality, strength, health, happiness and satisfaction, that are savory, rich, substantial and pleasing to the heart, are dear to the sāttvika person.
t.17.10: Food that is stale, tasteless, putrid and left overnight, and that which is leftover and impure, is dear to the tāmasic person.
t.17.9: Foods that are bitter, sour, salty, excessively hot, pungent, dry and burning are dear to the passionate person; they bring pain, grief and disease.
t.17.11: That sacrifice which is offered according to the scriptural injunction by those who do not desire its fruit, having fixed the mind on the thought that it ought simply to be offered, is sāttvika.
t.17.12: But that which is offered with an eye to its fruit, and also for the sake of ostentation, O best of the Bharatas, know that sacrifice to be rājasic.
t.17.13: A sacrifice performed without regard to the scriptural injunctions, in which no food is distributed, which is devoid of sacred mantras, offers no gifts to the priests, and lacks faith, they declare to be of the nature of tamas.
t.17.15: Speech that causes no agitation, that is truthful, pleasant and beneficial, and also the regular practice of sacred recitation, is called austerity of speech.
t.17.14: Worship of the gods, the twice-born, the teachers and the wise, purity, uprightness, celibacy and non-violence: this is called austerity of the body.
t.17.16: Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-restraint, and purity of one's inner being: this is called austerity of the mind.
t.17.17: That threefold austerity, practiced with supreme faith by steadfast men who do not crave its fruit, they call sāttvika.
t.17.18: Austerity that is performed for the sake of gaining respect, honor and reverence, and with ostentation, is here declared to be rājasa, unsteady and impermanent.
t.17.19: That austerity which is performed out of a deluded notion, with torture of oneself, or for the purpose of destroying another, is declared to be tāmasa.
t.17.20: The gift that is given with the thought "it ought to be given," to one who does no service in return, at the proper place and time and to a worthy recipient, that gift is held to be sāttvika.
t.17.21: But that gift which is given for the sake of a return favor, or again with an eye to its fruit, and which is given grudgingly, is held to be rājasa.
t.17.22: That gift which is given at the wrong place and time, and to unworthy recipients, without respect and with contempt, is declared to be tāmasa.
t.17.23: "Oṃ Tat Sat": this is remembered as the threefold designation of Brahman. By it were ordained of old the Brāhmaṇas, the Vedas and the sacrifices.
t.17.24: Therefore, uttering "Om," the expounders of Brahman always undertake their acts of sacrifice, giving, and austerity as enjoined by the scriptural rules.
t.17.25: Uttering "tat" and without aiming at the fruit, those who long for liberation perform the various acts of sacrifice and austerity and the acts of giving.
t.17.26: This word "sat" is used in the sense of reality and in the sense of goodness; likewise, O Pārtha, the word "sat" is applied to a praiseworthy deed.
t.17.27: Steadfastness in sacrifice, in austerity and in giving is also called "sat"; and any action done for that purpose is likewise designated "sat."
t.17.28: Whatever is offered in sacrifice, given, or practised as austerity, or otherwise done without faith, is called asat, O Pārtha; it is of no avail either after death or here.
